meal: Congee with salted egg and pickled vegetables
swap: Plain congee with a fresh egg, ginger, scallion and white pepper; keep pickles to a spoonful on the side
why: Salted egg and pickles carry most of the salt
portion: Your usual bowl of congee; keep the salted egg and pickles to a small side dish instead of mixing them in

meal: Stir-fry with soy sauce and oyster sauce
swap: Use about half the sauce and add garlic, ginger, chili and a splash of rice vinegar; add sauce at the end so it stays on the surface
why: Fresh aromatics give flavor without salt
portion: Fill half the plate with the stir-fried vegetables, then the meat or tofu, then rice

swap: Have a small bowl, eat the solids, salt lightly at the table; check with your care team before adding medicinal herbs
why: Long-simmered broth pulls potassium and salt into the liquid
portion: A small rice bowl of soup, not a big bowl, and eat the meat and vegetables from the pot

meal: Dim sum with soy dipping sauce
swap: Choose steamed har gow, vegetable dumplings or steamed fish; dip lightly or skip the soy; tea or water instead of soda
why: Steamed beats fried, and dipping sauces add a lot of salt
portion: Share the baskets and order one plate of steamed greens for the table

meal: Panda Express orange chicken with chow mein
swap: Grilled teriyaki chicken with sauce on the side, or string bean chicken, with steamed white rice
why: Less breading, sugar and salt than orange chicken and chow mein
portion: A one-entree plate with steamed rice instead of a two-entree plate

swap: Use a third to half the seasoning packet and add an egg, cabbage, bean sprouts and scallion
why: The packet is the main salt source
portion: One packet makes one meal; add an egg and a big handful of cabbage to the same bowl

swap: Pick a clear, mild broth, don't drink the broth, choose fresh meat and tofu over fish balls, dip in garlic, scallion and vinegar
why: Broth gets saltier as it cooks down, and processed balls are salty
portion: Fill your bowl with meat, tofu and vegetables from the pot and keep the broth in the pot

swap: Enjoy the noodles, meat and herbs, leave about half the broth, add lime, basil and bean sprouts, go light on hoisin
why: Most of the salt is in the broth
portion: Order the regular size, not the large, and leave about half the broth

swap: Fire-grilled chicken breast with the skin off, corn tortillas and a little salsa; go light on beans and skip cheese if your care team limits potassium or phosphorus
why: Grilled chicken is a good base; sides and cheese add salt, potassium and phosphorus
portion: A two-piece chicken meal with one side, not two

meal: Chipotle burrito with cheese, beans and guacamole
swap: A bowl with white rice, chicken or sofritas, fajita veggies and mild salsa; skip queso; if your care team limits potassium or phosphorus, go light on beans, guac and cheese
why: Cheese, beans and avocado add phosphorus and potassium; the tortilla adds salt
portion: A bowl gives you the same fillings without the big tortilla; one scoop of rice

meal: Enchiladas with canned sauce and cheese
swap: Make the sauce from dried chiles and garlic, use half the cheese, rinse canned beans, serve with cabbage slaw
why: Canned sauce and cheese are the big salt and phosphorus sources
portion: Two enchiladas with a big scoop of cabbage slaw instead of three

swap: Use half the soy sauce and more vinegar, garlic, bay leaf and black pepper; serve with white rice and sauteed cabbage
why: Vinegar and garlic carry the flavor with less soy
portion: A normal piece of chicken, a scoop of rice and a side of sauteed cabbage; spoon on less of the sauce

swap: Use fresh tamarind or less of the mix packet and leave some broth; if your care team limits potassium, choose radish, green beans and cabbage over taro and leafy greens
why: The mix packet is salty and some vegetables are high in potassium
portion: Eat the meat and vegetables and leave some of the soup in the bowl

swap: Teriyaki chicken or egg musubi with a light homemade sauce
why: Canned meats are high in salt and phosphate additives
portion: One musubi as a snack, with cucumber slices, rather than two or three

swap: Grill unmarinated or lightly marinated meat, wrap in lettuce, keep kimchi and dipping sauces to small portions
why: Marinades, kimchi and ssamjang add up fast
portion: Wrap each bite in lettuce and keep kimchi and banchan to small tastes

meal: Potato curry or palak (spinach) with dal
swap: Keep the spices, lemon and dal; if your care team limits potassium, try cauliflower, cabbage or green bean sabzi in place of potato or spinach, and a smaller bowl of dal
why: Potatoes, spinach and lentils are high in potassium, which matters if your blood potassium runs high
portion: Rice or roti, one vegetable dish, and dal in a small bowl

meal: Sushi with miso soup and soy sauce
swap: Skip the miso soup, dip lightly, choose salmon, tuna or cucumber rolls with pickled ginger
why: Miso and soy sauce carry most of the salt
portion: One or two rolls with pickled ginger; pour a little soy into the dish rather than filling it

meal: Big Mac, fries and a cola
swap: A plain hamburger or grilled chicken sandwich without cheese, apple slices, and water or sparkling water
why: Processed cheese and dark cola add phosphorus; fries add potassium and salt
portion: Kids' or small size fries, if any, and water to drink

swap: Thin crust, half the cheese, peppers, onions and mushrooms instead of pepperoni; one or two slices with a side salad
why: Cheese and cured meats are high in salt and phosphorus
portion: One or two slices with a side salad, then put the box away

swap: Grilled or roasted chicken with the skin off, with coleslaw or green beans
why: Breading and skin hold most of the salt
portion: Keep the chicken; take off the skin and add a vegetable side

swap: Fresh roasted chicken with lettuce, cucumber, peppers and onion, oil and vinegar instead of cheese
why: Deli meats have salt and phosphate additives
portion: A 6-inch, not a footlong, with extra vegetables

meal: Frozen lasagna or mac and cheese
swap: Pick a frozen meal labeled lower sodium, eat a smaller portion and add steamed frozen green beans or cauliflower
why: Cheese-heavy frozen meals are high in salt and phosphorus
portion: Half the tray, with a bowl of steamed vegetables beside it

swap: Thin-crust veggie pizza, half portion, add a side salad
why: Less cheese and no cured meat
portion: Half the pizza and a side salad

swap: Steam or boil instead of pan-fry, dip in black vinegar with ginger instead of soy
why: Vinegar and ginger keep the flavor with less salt
portion: A plate of dumplings with a side of stir-fried greens

swap: Homemade soup or a low-sodium version, in a smaller bowl; watch labels for potassium chloride
why: Regular canned soup is very salty
portion: A small bowl, not the whole can, with crackers that say unsalted

swap: A smaller scoop topped with berries, or frozen grapes
why: You still get a treat, with less dairy phosphorus and sugar
portion: A small scoop in a small bowl, topped with berries

swap: Unsalted popcorn, unsalted pretzels or rice crackers
why: Same crunch with far less salt
portion: Pour a small bowl instead of eating from the bag

swap: Sparkling water with lime, or unsweetened iced tea
why: Dark colas contain phosphoric acid
portion: If you have a soda, a small can, not a large cup

swap: Smaller size, 25 to 50 percent sugar, fewer pearls
why: Cuts sugar and milk while keeping the treat
portion: The regular or small size, shared or saved for a treat day

meal: Bananas or oranges as a snack
swap: Apples, berries, grapes or pineapple
why: Lower-potassium fruits, if your care team limits potassium
portion: One small piece of fruit at a time

meal: Taiwanese beef noodle soup (niu rou mian)
swap: Keep the noodles, beef and greens; leave most of the broth; ask for extra bok choy; go easy on the pickled mustard greens at the table
why: The long-braised soy broth and pickled greens carry most of the salt
portion: Same bowl with fewer noodles: let the beef and extra greens fill it out

meal: Taiwanese braised pork rice (lu rou fan)
swap: Ask for less sauce over the rice, add a plate of blanched greens and a plain boiled egg instead of the soy-braised egg
why: The soy and sugar braise soaks into the rice
portion: A small bowl of rice with a side plate of blanched greens

meal: Taiwanese salt and pepper fried chicken (yan su ji)
swap: Ask for less seasoning powder, add fried basil and garlic for flavor, and get a side of blanched vegetables
why: The seasoning powder and the batter hold most of the salt
portion: Share one small bag and add a vegetable side

swap: Dip in black vinegar with ginger slivers instead of soy sauce; add a plate of stir-fried pea shoots or green beans
why: The soup inside each dumpling is seasoned broth
portion: Share a basket and add a vegetable dish instead of a second basket

swap: Use half the chili bean paste (doubanjiang) and more Sichuan peppercorn, garlic, ginger and scallion; serve with rice and a plain vegetable
why: Fermented bean paste is very salty; peppercorn and aromatics keep the numbing heat
portion: Keep the tofu and pork, and pair it with a plain vegetable rather than a second saucy dish

swap: Poached chicken with ginger-scallion sauce and a little chili, cucumber on the side, skip the soup; ask for plain rice if they have it
why: The rice is cooked in salted chicken stock and the soup adds more
portion: Your usual chicken, a smaller scoop of rice and extra cucumber

swap: Ask for the soup on the side or leave most of it; add a plate of gai lan with oyster sauce on the side
why: Most of the salt is in the broth
portion: Eat the wontons and noodles and leave most of the soup

swap: Ask for the sauce on the side, add steamed gai lan, or get half char siu and half roast chicken
why: The glaze and the extra sauce poured on the rice are salty and sweet
portion: Keep the meat portion, make some of it plain roast chicken, and add greens

swap: Egg, scallion, cabbage and bean sprouts with a small splash of soy at the end; use a little or no Chinese sausage (lap cheong)
why: Soy sauce and cured sausage are the main salt sources
portion: Half rice, half egg and vegetables in the same bowl

swap: Steam with lots of ginger and scallion, sizzle with hot oil, and pour on a spoonful of soy sauce mixed with water
why: The hot oil and aromatics carry the flavor, so less soy is needed
portion: Your usual piece of fish with rice and a green vegetable

swap: Fill with fresh pork, mushrooms and chestnuts; use half or none of the salted egg yolk and less soy in the marinade
why: Salted egg yolk and cured meat carry most of the salt
portion: One zongzi with a vegetable side instead of two

swap: Make it at home with less salt in the dough and plenty of scallion and white pepper; dip in black vinegar
why: Store and restaurant pancakes are salted in the dough and on top
portion: A wedge or two as a side, not the whole pancake as a meal

swap: Choose grilled chicken or lemongrass pork over cold cuts and pate; extra cucumber, cilantro and jalapeno; go light on the soy or Maggi drizzle
why: Cold cuts and pate have salt and phosphate additives
portion: Half now and half later if the roll is big

meal: Grilled pork vermicelli bowl (bun thit nuong)
swap: Pour on half the fish sauce dressing, add extra lettuce, herbs and cucumber, and share the fried egg roll
why: The dressing and the egg roll hold most of the salt
portion: Same bowl with more herbs and lettuce and half the dressing

swap: Use less kimchi and gochujang, add more tofu, onion and mushroom, and eat the solids rather than the broth
why: Kimchi and chili paste are both very salty
portion: A small bowl of stew with rice and a plain egg side dish

swap: Ask for the gochujang on the side and add a little at a time; extra vegetables and a fried egg
why: Most of the salt is in the chili paste
portion: A smaller scoop of rice with more vegetables and egg

swap: Eat the noodles, egg and meat, leave most of the broth, and ask for extra bean sprouts and scallion
why: Ramen broth is one of the saltiest restaurant foods
portion: Regular size, not large; leave most of the broth

swap: Sauce on the side, extra steamed vegetables, white rice
why: The teriyaki sauce is salty and sweet
portion: Half the rice and double the steamed vegetables

swap: Ask for less sauce, extra bean sprouts and lime, and crushed peanuts on the side
why: The sauce has fish sauce, sugar and tamarind
portion: Share one plate and add a cucumber salad

swap: Eat the chicken and vegetables over rice and leave some of the curry sauce in the bowl; add fresh Thai basil
why: The sauce holds the salt, and coconut milk adds potassium
portion: Spoon the curry over rice instead of eating it like soup

swap: Use half the soy and oyster sauce, add more cabbage, carrots and chicken, and squeeze calamansi at the table
why: Soy and oyster sauce are the main salt sources
portion: Plate it half noodles, half vegetables and chicken

swap: Season the filling with garlic, onion and pepper instead of extra soy, air-fry or bake, and go light on the sweet chili sauce
why: The filling seasoning and dipping sauce add up
portion: A few pieces beside rice and a vegetable dish, not a whole plate

swap: Make homemade garlic chicken or pork with vinegar, garlic and a little sugar; garlic rice with less salt; add cucumber
why: Store-bought cured meats have salt and phosphate additives
portion: One or two pieces of meat, a smaller scoop of garlic rice and an egg

swap: Use fresh pork or chicken, rinsed hominy and homemade broth; load up on cabbage, radish, onion, lime and oregano
why: Canned broth, canned hominy and seasoning mixes carry the salt
portion: A smaller bowl of broth with lots of cabbage and toppings

swap: Corn tortillas, grilled meat, onion, cilantro, lime and salsa verde; go light on cheese and crema; if your care team limits potassium, a small spoon of guacamole
why: Cheese, crema and refried beans add salt; avocado adds potassium
portion: Two or three tacos with cabbage slaw instead of a full plate of rice and beans

swap: Make the masa with less salt and homemade broth, fill with chicken and green chile, and serve with a salad
why: Masa mixes and store broth are salty, and baking powder can add phosphorus
portion: One or two tamales with a vegetable side

swap: Choose chicken or loroco with less cheese, and add extra curtido (cabbage slaw)
why: Cheese is the main source of salt and phosphorus
portion: Two pupusas with a big scoop of curtido

swap: Try tandoori chicken or chicken tikka with plain rice or roti, and a small cucumber raita
why: The cream sauce and buttered naan are rich in salt and dairy
portion: Share one curry and eat it with rice or one roti, not two naan

swap: Use whole spices, saffron, mint and fried onion for flavor and less salt; serve with cucumber raita and a salad
why: Spices carry biryani, so salt can come down
portion: One plate with a cucumber-onion salad instead of seconds

swap: If your care team limits potassium, choose onion or cauliflower pakora over potato samosa; air-fry at home; mint-cilantro chutney
why: Potato filling is high in potassium and the pastry is salted
portion: One or two as a snack, not a meal

swap: Ask for garlic sauce and tahini on the side, extra salad, and just a few pickles
why: Pickles, sauces and the marinade add salt
portion: Keep the chicken; choose rice or pita, not both, and fill the rest with salad

swap: Make hummus with more lemon, garlic and cumin and less salt; dip cucumber and bell pepper strips along with the pita
why: Store hummus and pita are salted; chickpeas add potassium and phosphorus, which only matters if your care team limits them
portion: A few spoonfuls as a dip, not a bowl

meal: Greek salad with feta and olives
swap: Half the feta and olives, more cucumber, onion and bell pepper, olive oil, lemon and oregano
why: Feta and olives are the salty part
portion: A big bowl of vegetables with a small sprinkle of feta

swap: Use half or none of the bouillon cube and more onion, thyme, curry powder and bay leaf; if your care team limits potassium, use less tomato paste
why: Bouillon cubes are very salty; tomato paste adds potassium
portion: A smaller scoop of jollof with chicken and a cabbage or cucumber salad

meal: Soul food plate (fried catfish, greens, mac and cheese)
swap: Cornmeal-crusted catfish baked or pan-fried, greens cooked with onion, garlic, vinegar and pepper flakes instead of ham hock, and a small scoop of mac and cheese
why: Ham hock, cheese sauce and seasoned breading carry the salt and phosphorus
portion: Fish as the main, a small scoop of mac and cheese, and a vegetable side

swap: Pull off the skin, or roast your own chicken with lemon, garlic and herbs; check labels for 'solution' or 'broth' added to the meat
why: Many store chickens are injected with salt water and phosphates
portion: Keep your usual amount of chicken; take the skin off

swap: Eat the fruit whole instead, such as berries, apple or pineapple; if you love smoothies, a small glass with a meal
why: Blending breaks down the fiber, so sugar and potassium hit faster; on dialysis it counts as fluid
portion: A small glass, not a large cup

swap: Use a splash of regular milk or a creamer with no 'phos' words in the ingredients
why: Many creamers contain phosphate additives, which are absorbed easily
portion: Your usual cup; on dialysis it counts toward fluids

swap: Eggs with herbs and pepper, toast with unsalted butter, and a homemade chicken patty seasoned with sage instead of bacon or sausage
why: Bacon and breakfast sausage are cured with salt and phosphates
portion: Eggs and toast as the base; save bacon for weekends

swap: Dressing on the side, skip croutons, bacon bits and cheese, and add grilled chicken
why: Dressings, toppings and pre-salted greens add up
portion: Dip your fork in the dressing instead of pouring it on
